s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Diffusely enhancing lesion on thoracic spine MRI
Expansile bony lesion on CT of thoracic spine
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Unable to walk more than a few steps
Diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 on MRI
Near-circumferential epidural extension causing severe cord compression
Expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body with extension into left pedicle and posterior elements on CT
No evidence of primary malignancy on CT scans of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, within normal limits

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance and spinal cord compression with a diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1

shortlist.label: Metastatic lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body with extension into left pedicle and posterior elements

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Midline location and aggressive bony destruction at T1

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body with spinal cord compression

shortlist.label: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile and destructive bony lesion at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension

raw.rationale: The expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements, along with the diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 on MRI and the absence of evidence of primary malignancy, is most consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare bone tumor that can cause spinal cord compression.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as bone pain, fevers, night sweats, and weight loss, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer
rejected.why: Patient has no history of smoking or known malignancy, and CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a solitary bone lesion and may have systemic symptoms, but the imaging findings and lack of systemic symptoms in this case make it less likely

rejected.label: Metastatic renal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with a known history of renal cell carcinoma, and CT scans of the abdomen and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy
